clue.text: Heave line back and start to mix bait

parts.note: to lug is to heave or haul something heavy

indicators.note: back tells us the word for line is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a row is a line of things

indicators.note: start to points at the opening letter of the word mix

explanation.surface: An angler hauls in the line and begins mixing up some groundbait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROW into WOR; 'start to' takes M from mix.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing sea worm is dug from beaches as an angler's bait.

clue.text: Some underclothing Jack wears itches

indicators.note: wears means the yearning word goes round the name like a garment

parts.note: longs means yearns or itches for something
Jack is a pet form of the name John

explanation.surface: A man called Jack puts on underwear that makes him scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itches' looks like the underwear's effect, but it is the verb longs, meaning yearns; 'wears' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long underpants reaching to the ankles are a warm undergarment.

clue.text: Good woman's family in a bit of a pickle

parts.note: her is the possessive of a woman
kin means family

explanation.surface: A decent woman's relatives find themselves in some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a pickle' looks like trouble but means one pickled item.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pickled cucumber is a piece of pickle.

clue.text: Find one's way East three times by river

parts.note: the Orient is the East
E again for East, the third time

explanation.surface: Heading east three times along a river to get one's bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three times' asks for East thrice: ORIENT, E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in orienteering navigates with map and compass across country.

clue.text: Blow warmer

definitions.meaning: to blow a chance is to bungle it, as when dropping a catch
a fur tube for keeping the hands or ears warm

explanation.definitionFit: To bungle a catch is a sporting sense, and the fur hand-tube is a winter warmer.

clue.text: Elementary ingredient for making chips

parts.note: elementary hints at a chemical element, and the chips are microchips rather than fried potatoes

explanation.surface: A cookery tip about the basic thing you need for frying chips.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is false: 'Elementary' means a chemical element and 'chips' are computer chips.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical element is the semiconductor from which microchips are made.

clue.text: Dresser following a hard design?

parts.note: a dresser seems a fashion person or furniture, but here is a worker who dresses rock to an architect's plan

explanation.surface: A fashion stylist working to a tough brief.
explanation.walkthrough: To dress stone is to shape and face it; the 'hard' material is the rock itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts and shapes building blocks of rock to a design.

clue.text: Learners have hidden copy in fold of jacket

indicators.note: have hidden means the two learner letters enclose the copying word

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate, so two learners are LL
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Learner drivers conceal a crib sheet in their jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark British learner drivers, so two learners give two Ls; 'have hidden' is the container signal, not a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded-back part at the front of a jacket below the collar.

clue.text: Oral examiner put things in black and white

definitions.text: put things in black and white

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for examiner is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a checker is one who examines or inspects

explanation.surface: A spoken-test examiner writes down the results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black and white' suggests writing, but means a checkerboard pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark with a pattern of alternating squares, like a chessboard.

clue.text: Vote against taking in the races — that's smart

indicators.note: taking in means the vote word surrounds the races

parts.note: a nay is a vote against
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Opposing a day at the races is the clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone neat and stylishly dressed.

clue.text: Blemishes occurring when a vein ruptures

indicators.note: a vein that ruptures breaks apart, so its letters with the a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Skin marks that appear when a blood vessel bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruptures' rearranges A VEIN; 'occurring when' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are birthmarks or moles, the plural of a Latin medical word for a skin mark.

clue.text: Most relaxed, in spite of LP being remixed

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is at their most laid-back even though their record is getting a remix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being remixed' rearranges SPITE OF LP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy can mean limp and loose, so the superlative describes the most slack or relaxed.

clue.text: Jester's job — most of it with monarch

indicators.note: most of it means drop the final letter of the word just mentioned

parts.note: the word job itself, from the definition's own phrase, reused as wordplay
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A court fool's work, much of which is done alongside the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of it' drops the last letter of 'job', leaving JO.
explanation.definitionFit: Making jests and quips is exactly what a court jester does for a living.

clue.text: In Paris I may have a terrible feeling of envy

parts.note: je is French for I
lousy means very bad or terrible

explanation.surface: A traveller in France admits to a dreadful bout of envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may have' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment at another's advantages is a synonym for envy.

clue.text: Player's equipment found in press enclosure

parts.note: to squeeze is to press
a box is an enclosure

explanation.surface: A footballer's kit turns up in the press box at the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion or concertina, the instrument a musical player squeezes.

clue.text: So the Stag's opposite the church?

parts.note: a stag party for a groom is matched by a hen party for a bride
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A question about whether the stag party has gathered across from the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Stag and hen parties are British pre-wedding nights out for groom and bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean therefore, introducing a consequence.

clue.text: Rely, oddly, on a couple of pints every few months

indicators.note: on places the jumbled word after the measure of pints

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters of rely are put in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone depends, strangely, on a couple of pints of beer every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is an anagram signal here, not a call for odd letters, which would give only two letters; 'on' places the result after the pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening four times a year occurs at three-month intervals.

clue.text: This fishing gear won't get in tangles

indicators.note: tangles suggests a knotted mess, so the letters are snarled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boast that this net never gets snarled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangles' rearranges WON'T GET IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A net dragged behind a boat to catch fish.

clue.text: What will the present be tomorrow?

definitions.text: What will the present be tomorrow?

parts.words: What will the present be tomorrow?
parts.note: the present means today rather than a gift, and by tomorrow today has become the day before

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a gift turns into the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but means the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today, which is what today will be once tomorrow arrives.

clue.text: Fantastic performer about to return in new production of Orpheus

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the rearranged title
a new production restages the opera, so its title letters are reworked
to return means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A brilliant singer is coming back to star in a fresh staging of Gluck's opera Orpheus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the word for about; 'in' sets it inside SUPHRO, the letters of ORPHEUS rearranged ('new production of'). Orpheus is an opera by Gluck.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book hero with fantastic powers is a performer of amazing feats.

clue.text: Fuss friend to give an opinion

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to assert or declare

explanation.surface: A mate makes a fuss about stating his views.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome fuss and bother is a synonym.

clue.text: Jack sets them a target — a small forest

definitions.meaning: in bowls the bowls themselves, called by this name, are rolled towards the small white ball, the jack
a wooded area smaller than a forest

explanation.walkthrough: Bowls is a lawn game where players roll weighted balls towards a small white target ball, the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: In bowls each player's ball is named after the timber it was made from, and a stretch of trees is a wood.

clue.text: Marginally question soundness of old American state

parts.note: Belize is a Central American country

explanation.surface: Casting doubt on the stability of a former American territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marginally' means in a margin: scholars marked doubtful passages with a dagger sign there.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking a doubtful passage with a dagger or obelus queries whether it is genuine.

clue.text: Force animal to sleep

parts.note: a bull is an animal
to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make a beast nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: To push through by intimidation is to steamroller or coerce, as a heavy earthmover does.

clue.text: Equivalent of taxi in Lancs town

parts.note: in a down light a taxi word read upwards appears backwards with up after it

explanation.surface: A cab ride equivalent in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in a down light, CAB going up reads BAC, and 'up' says so; Lancs is Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a small town in the Rossendale valley of Lancashire.

clue.text: About to interrupt father, took a chance

indicators.note: to interrupt means the about word breaks into the father word

parts.note: dad is father
re means about

explanation.surface: A child gambles by cutting in while dad is talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' is the container signal: the short word for about breaks into the father word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ventured or risked doing something bold.

clue.text: Queen houses old lover in adjoining building

indicators.note: houses means the queen's name contains the other piece

parts.note: Anne was a queen of Great Britain
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A queen puts up her former sweetheart in a property next door.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension or outbuilding attached to a main building.

clue.text: Water spirit that's invisible in seaweed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Water spirit that's invisible in seaweed' parses as KELPIE less IE (that's) giving KELP, defined by seaweed; it cannot give the held answer PEEP, which is not marked as a model guess.
annotationWithheld.clue: Water spirit that's invisible in seaweed

clue.text: Message about deliveries qualifying for insurance?

indicators.note: about means the message word goes round the deliveries

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

explanation.surface: A note asking whether parcel deliveries can be insured.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an over is a set of six balls bowled. 'about' is the container signal, the message going round the deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk that can be insured is one an insurer can protect against.

clue.text: Girl in the classical stream, perhaps?

definitions.text: Girl in the classical stream, perhaps?

parts.words: Girl in the classical stream, perhaps?
parts.note: the classical stream sounds like a school class, but it is a river of Greek myth with a female spirit living in it

explanation.surface: A pupil placed in the classics set at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The school 'stream' is a false trail: this is a river nymph of classical mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph is the female spirit of a river or spring.

clue.text: Almost demonstrate neat contradiction

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to parade is to march in a demonstration or display
neat is an old word for cattle, one of which is an ox

explanation.surface: Barely making a tidy protest that contradicts itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts PARADE to PARAD. 'neat' is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement that may yet be true.

clue.text: Corrupt lay arbitrator reaching dodgy' conclusion

parts.note: to lay is to put down
a ref, short for referee, arbitrates in a game

indicators.note: conclusion points to the final letter of the word dodgy

explanation.surface: A bent amateur judge reaches a dubious verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion' takes Y, the last letter of dodgy; 'reaching' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot or decay, as corrupted flesh does.
